3LCD: Epson's 3-chip tech — no rainbow effect, accurate colors
4ms input lag: delay between controller and screen — under 20ms is great for gaming
ABS/ASA: tough plastics needing heat — for functional parts, not just toys
AMS: Bambu's auto filament changer — prints multi-color without you swapping spools
Acceleration: how fast the print head gets up to speed — higher = faster prints
Bed Leveling: auto-calibrates the print surface — no manual knob-twisting
Brightness: higher lumens = watchable with lights on
Build Volume: max object size you can print — bigger = larger parts in one go
Carbon fiber: filament mixed with carbon strands — super stiff, needs hardened nozzle
Chamber: heated enclosure keeps temp stable — prevents warping on tough plastics
Contrast: difference between darkest black and brightest white — higher = punchier image
CoreXY: fast printer design where the head moves on belts — speed without shaking
DLP: chip with tiny mirrors — sharp image, but some see rainbow flashes
Enclosure: closed box around printer — keeps heat in for warp-free ABS/ASA
FlexiArm: Roborock's extending mop arm — reaches corners the round body can't
HDR10+: better colors and brightness in movies — like HDR, but smarter
Hotend: the part that melts filament — all-metal = hotter materials possible
ISO lumens: brightness standard — 2500+ works in dim rooms, 3000+ handles some daylight
Input Lag: gaming delay — 4ms is esports-grade, 50ms+ feels sluggish
Klipper: open-source printer firmware — tinker-friendly, very fast
Laser: light source lasting 20,000+ hours — no bulb replacements
Lens shift: move the image without moving the projector — flexible installation
LiDAR: laser sensor that maps the room/print bed — for navigation and auto-calibration
Mop wash: dock cleans the mop pads with hot water — you don't touch dirty pads
Multi-color: print in several colors in one job — needs AMS or similar system
Nozzle Temp: max heat of the extruder — 300°C+ unlocks engineering plastics
Obstacle avoidance: dodges cables, shoes, pet bowls instead of ramming them
Pa: suction power unit — 20,000Pa is strong, 35,000Pa is the current max
Rainbow effect: color flashes some people see on DLP projectors — 3LCD doesn't have it
Self-empty: dock sucks dust into a bag — you empty it monthly, not daily
Speed: how fast filament gets laid down — 500mm/s is very fast
StarSight: Roborock's navigation without a spinning tower — slimmer body
Suction: cleaning power — higher Pa = better on carpets and pet hair
Throw ratio: distance needed for a big image — lower = bigger screen from closer
Vormax: Dreame's suction tech branding — their top-tier motor
Polyester: Plastic fiber. Melted petroleum spun into thread — cheap, durable, doesn't breathe
Nylon: Plastic fiber, silk-like. Strong and stretchy, but traps odor
Spandex: Rubber-like stretch fiber. The 'stretch' in stretchy clothes — 3-5% is plenty
Elastane: Same as spandex (Lycra is a brand name). The stretch fiber in everything
Cotton combed: Natural fiber, breathable. Combed = smoother yarn, less pilling
Modal: Wood-pulp fiber (usually beech). Softer than cotton, resists shrinking
Merino wool: Fine sheep wool. Warm, naturally odor-resistant — the premium natural pick
Bamboo fiber: Marketing name — usually just rayon made from bamboo pulp, not magical
Rayon: Wood-pulp fiber processed with chemicals. Soft and drapey, wrinkles fast
Viscose: Same as rayon. Soft plant-based fiber, weak when wet
GSM: Fabric weight in grams per square meter — higher = thicker and heavier
Thread count: Threads per square inch. Above 400 is mostly marketing
Pilling: Those little fabric balls on clothes — shorter/cheaper fibers pill more
Moisture-wicking: Pulls sweat off your skin. Polyester does this; cotton just soaks and stays wet
Tagless: Printed label instead of sewn tag — no neck itch
Pima cotton: Long-staple cotton — softer and more durable than regular cotton
Odor-resistant: Treated fabric or natural fiber (merino) that stinks less — treatments wash out over time
